title: CrowdDeck
summary: An open-source venue runtime that runs a DJ deck engine and a TouchTunes-style crowd request jukebox on one scheduler, library and clock, for venues that are a jukebox by day and a DJ room by night.

narrative.problem: Every DJ application surveyed scores effectively zero on crowd participation, and every jukebox platform scores effectively zero on performance capability, yet real venues need both on a schedule. Existing open-source jukeboxes also depend on a host's consumer Spotify account, which conveys no public-performance rights.
narrative.decision: Writes the engine contract (CDEP, NDJSON over a local socket) first and keeps the planned GPL-2.0-or-later Mixxx engine behind a hard process boundary from the Apache-2.0 core, proven replaceable by a conformant stub engine and a browser Web Audio engine.
narrative.tradeoff: The project ships as two separate downloads and every engine call crosses an IPC boundary, so its latency budgets depend on measurements still outstanding; the split-licence position is accepted risk, with no legal review obtained or planned.
narrative.limitation: The build is in progress at 76 of 91 stories. The venue clients (patron, DJ console, display) still run on the silent stub engine, the native Mixxx engine is not built, and latency is measured only on WASAPI; other platforms need real audio and MIDI hardware.
narrative.caveat: The live deck plays openly licensed music entirely in the browser and uploads nothing; the venue clients still use a stub engine that produces no sound.

images.caption: The core idea: crowd requests go to the DJ's staging lane, not straight to the output.
